reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output shape for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.

The cited paragraphs (§1(c) facility/system-access, §3(b) invoicing detail, §4(c) license grant) contain no audit, inspection or verification right running against Customer; the only system-access language constrains Contractor's access to Company systems under Company policies, which benefits us.

Because the AUDIT rule is protective of Customer, the total absence of a vendor audit right is at least as good as the preferred position, so raising a redline would risk conceding an audit right we do not currently grant — treating this as compliant (internal evidence only) rather than 'missing' is the correct call.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is correctly explained as an artefact of there being no audit clause to match, not evidence of a deviation; the rationale also flags the SOW watch-item and the fallback limits for future use.
